subject: Animation
title: The Multiplane Camera: Depth in 2D
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Multiplane Camera: Depth in 2D.

hook.text: Disney invented the multiplane camera in 1937 to give flat 2D animation the illusion of depth.

buildup.text: The camera filmed through layers of glass, each holding different elements at different distances.

discovery.text: Moving the layers at different speeds created parallax — foreground moved fast, background moved slowly.

twist.text: The multiplane camera cost $70,000 to build in 1937 — equivalent to over $1.4 million today.

climax.text: The multiplane camera gave Snow White a visual depth that no other animated film had achieved before.

punchline.text: Layers of glass gave flat drawings the illusion of a deep world.

quiz.question: How did the multiplane camera create depth in 2D animation?
options: It used 3D glasses for the audience
It filmed through layers of glass at different distances, moving them at different speeds for parallax
It projected images onto curved screens
